title: Cyber Resilience Act: can you still sell your products in the EU after 11 December 2027?
short: Report exploited flaws within 24 hours now, and give every product a risk assessment, SBOM, support period and CE marking by 11 December 2027.
answer: Be ready now to report an actively exploited vulnerability or severe incident in any product on the EU market within 24 hours. Before 11 December 2027, give every product a class, a support period, a risk assessment, an SBOM and technical documentation, so it can carry the CE marking.
audience: Companies that make, import or distribute hardware or software sold in the EU, and open-source stewards

blocks.title: If you only do five things

items.title: Be able to report within 24 hours.
items.text: Reporting has applied since 11 September 2026, also to products sold before the CRA applies in full and after their support ends[^guide]. Name an owner and a deputy with EU Login accounts and MFA, and decide which CSIRT you report to[^srpfaq].

items.title: Classify each product by its core functionality.
items.text: Match it against Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2392[^ir2392]. Default products may always self-assess; important and critical ones may need a notified body[^guide].

items.title: Set a support period per product.
items.text: At least 5 years unless the product is expected to be used for less, and longer if it lasts longer[^cra][^guide]. Show the end month and year at the point of sale[^cra].

items.title: Write the risk assessment first.
items.text: It decides which Annex I requirements apply and goes into the technical documentation[^cra]. Cover planned features too, so later updates aren't substantial modifications[^guide].

items.title: Run vulnerability handling as a process.
items.text: An SBOM per release, a disclosure policy and contact, and free security updates[^cra]. The supply chain and secure development sheets show how.

blocks.title: Are you in scope, and in which role?

items.title: Does it connect to a device or network?
items.text: Then the CRA covers it, with the remote data processing it needs to work[^cra]. Web apps used only in a browser, websites and SaaS are not products themselves[^guide].

items.title: Is it excluded?
items.text: Medical and diagnostic devices, motor vehicles, certified aviation products, marine equipment, identical spare parts and national security products are[^cra].

items.title: Do you supply it commercially?
items.text: Charging for it or for support beyond cost, monetizing it through other services or requiring personal data for other purposes counts, even if it's free[^cra]. Open source you don't monetize doesn't[^cra].

items.title: Are you an open-source steward?
items.text: Foundations and companies that systematically support non-monetized open source meant for commercial use are[^guide]. They need a documented security policy[^cra], report from December 2027[^srpfaq] and can't be fined[^cra].

items.title: Which role do you have?
items.text: Manufacturers sell under their own name; importers and distributors check the CE marking and documents first[^cra]. Rebranding or substantially modifying a product makes you its manufacturer[^cra].

blocks.title: Product classes and conformity assessment
items: **Default.** Anything not listed in Annexes III and IV. Self-assessment (module A) is always allowed[^guide].

**Important, class I.** 19 categories, such as identity and access management, browsers, password managers, antivirus, VPNs, operating systems, routers and smart home security products. Self-assess only with a cited harmonised standard, common specification or EU certificate applied in full; otherwise use a notified body[^cra].
**Important, class II.** Hypervisors, container runtimes, firewalls, intrusion detection and prevention systems and tamper-resistant chips. Always third party[^cra].

**Critical.** Hardware security boxes, smart meter gateways and smartcards: EU certification where a delegated act requires it, otherwise as class II[^cra]. The class of the whole product counts, not that of its components[^guide].
**No standard to lean on yet.** Only standards cited in the Official Journal give presumption of conformity[^cra]. ETSI's 17 product-specific drafts were in approval until mid-November 2026[^etsi].

blocks.title: Annex I in practice
items: **No known exploitable flaws at release.** Known means listed in the EU vulnerability database or another prominent one, or reported to you privately[^guide].
**Secure defaults.** A secure default configuration with a reset, access control, encryption of stored and transmitted data, minimal data and a way to delete it all[^cra].
**Automatic security updates on by default.** With an opt-out, notifications and a way to postpone[^cra].

**An SBOM per release.** Machine-readable, covering at least top-level dependencies[^cra]. BSI TR-03183-2 asks for CycloneDX 1.6 or SPDX 3.0.1, with dependencies resolved through everything you ship[^tr2].
**One contact, reachable any way.** A single point of contact not limited to automated tools[^cra], plus a disclosure policy and a `security.txt`[^tr3].

**Free fixes, kept available.** Keep each security update available for 10 years or the rest of the support period, if longer[^cra]. For software, fixing only the latest version is fine if upgrading costs users nothing extra[^cra].
**Advisories and upstream reports.** Publish fixed flaws, in CSAF as the BSI recommends[^cra][^tr3], and report component flaws with your fix to their maintainer[^cra].

blocks.title: Reporting clocks since 11 September 2026
blocks.intro: Clocks start at reasonable certainty after a prompt first check[^guide]. Report once on ENISA's platform, in Germany to CERT-Bund, and tell affected users[^cra][^bsisrp].

items.name: Actively exploited vulnerability
items.scope: Reliable evidence that an attacker exploited a flaw in your product[^cra]; a public exploit isn't enough[^bsisrp].

steps.what: Early warning, with countries sold in
Final report, counted from the fix

items.name: Severe incident
items.scope: It harms the product's protection of data or functions, or could plant malicious code[^cra]. Ransomware at the maker counts if it can reach software, updates or keys[^bsisrp].

steps.what: Final report, counted from the notification

blocks.title: Documentation, CE marking and fines
items: **Technical documentation (Annex VII).** Architecture, vulnerability handling with SBOM and disclosure policy, risk assessment, support period reasons, standards, test reports and the declaration, kept 10 years or the support period, if longer[^cra]. The simplified form for micro and small firms isn't published yet[^ecmsme].
**EU declaration of conformity.** Follow Annex V, ship it or a simplified version with its web address, and issue one for all EU acts that need one[^cra].
**CE marking from 11 December 2027.** On the product, or the packaging and declaration; for software, on the declaration or its website[^cra].

**Fines up to €15 million or 2.5% of turnover.** For breaching Annex I or Articles 13 and 14; €10 million or 2% for most other duties. Micro and small manufacturers aren't fined for a late 24-hour early warning[^cra].

blocks.title: What you can skip
items: **Waiting for harmonised standards.** The risk assessment, SBOM, disclosure policy and update channel don't depend on them.
**Reporting every vulnerable dependency.** A component flaw that isn't reachable or exploited in your product isn't reportable[^guide]; report it upstream and fix it as usual.
**Redesigning products that already hold up.** Older designs need no change if the risk assessment shows adequate measures[^guide].
**Registering on ENISA's platform early.** ENISA asks you to register when you first report; with EU Login ready, it takes minutes[^srpfaq].

blocks.title: Mistakes that cost the most
items: **Counting on the transition for hardware.** Each unit placed on the market from 11 December 2027 must comply, even of an older model; software counts per version, when first offered[^guide].
**Picking the wrong CSIRT.** The notification may be invalidated and need resubmitting[^srpfaq].
**Rebranding without noticing.** Selling under your own name makes you the manufacturer, with all its duties[^cra].
**A 5-year support period by reflex.** The Commission says 5 years is a floor, not a default[^guide].

blocks.title: What changed in 2026
items: **Reporting went live on 11 September.** ENISA's platform is English only, has no API yet and its 72-hour counter can show reports overdue early[^srpfaq].
**The Commission published draft guidance on 27 July.** It covers scope, open source, substantial modification, support periods and reporting, and isn't binding[^guide].
**Germany is naming the BSI.** On 14 October the Bundestag's interior committee approved the bill making it market surveillance and notifying authority[^bthib].
**Radio equipment moves to the CRA.** The radio equipment cybersecurity delegated act is repealed from 11 December 2027[^dr339].
**The Digital Omnibus leaves the CRA alone.** It would only let a CRA severe incident report also count for NIS2[^omnibus].

blocks.title: What this looks like at your size

columns.title: Small team, no security staff
items: List every product and version you sell in the EU, with its class and support end date.
Write a one-page runbook: who reports, to which CSIRT, from which EU Login accounts.
Use ENISA's secure by design playbook for SMEs[^enisasbd] and BSI TR-03183-1[^tr] as checklists.

columns.title: Growing, with IT or security staff
items: Name a product security owner and ship an SBOM and advisories with every release.
For class I or II products, book a notified body now; Member States aim to have enough by 11 December 2026[^cra].
Document one product end to end, then reuse it for its variants[^guide].

columns.title: Enterprise or regulated
items: Build module H on your ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS, as BSI TR-03183-H shows[^tr].
Run CRA reports in your NIS2 incident process; the EU security laws sheet has those clocks.
Agree how importers and distributors pass on the vulnerabilities they must report to you[^cra].
